evidence.drag_guard_mouse_pen: Resolved. Mouse and pen give pointerleave with buttons!==0 while the button is held and the pointer leaves. CoachMic.tsx:145-147 and Composer.tsx:43 then clear recordPointerDown, and the main control also clears activationMode.
evidence.drag_guard_touch: Not resolved. Touch has implicit pointer capture, so no pointerleave fires while the finger is down. After pointerup and lostpointercapture, pointerout and pointerleave fire with buttons=0. That is the case the code deliberately keeps. A touch drag-off with no scroll (so no pointercancel) and no click still leaves recordPointerDown=true. The test at tap-control.test.tsx:155-175 fires a touch pointerLeave with buttons=1 before pointerUp. A real touch browser does not send that sequence, so the test proves the mouse case only. The impact is unchanged from the prior finding: low, a label problem only. The secondary Send stays reachable, and the next click on any composer action clears the guard. This follows from the requested trade-off, which keeps the guard on buttons=0.
evidence.autonomous_review_gate: Resolved. publish (CoachMic.tsx:100-103) sets reviewNeeded on every locked→unlocked transition that is not a manual Stop and has text: silence, error, max-duration and pagehide. mode puts review ahead of send (:132). send() refuses while reviewNeeded (use-composer-input.ts:17). The secondary Send is hidden (Composer.tsx:39), which also blocks textarea Enter. Acknowledging Review only moves the control to Send (:163) and never sends in the same click. Tests at tap-control.test.tsx:177-274 cover pointer, keyboard Enter, pointerdown after completion, failure, max-duration and pagehide.
evidence.manual_stop_path: The Stop branch sets manualStop=true (:165). The unlock publish then gives reviewNeeded=false and resets manualStop, so the control goes busy, then Send. The detail>1 guard (:161) and the latch cover the second click of a double tap.
evidence.latch_pointer: pointerdown records the committed mode. If a re-render between pointerdown and click changes the mode, the click is dropped (:157-160). Stop/busy → Review/Send is blocked, and the latch resets on click, cancel, active leave and blur.
evidence.latch_keyboard: Enter fires click during keydown, so the latch is set and read in the same task. Space fires click on keyup, so a Stop keydown held across an automatic completion gives a keyup click that the mismatch drops. Repeated keydown is prevented (:152).
evidence.lifecycle: pagehide and visibilitychange call hold.cancel(), then abandon, then an unlocked publish, which sets Review when the box has text. Unmount calls cancel as well. The busy/settling state is aria-disabled and no click branch acts on it.

new_concrete_bugs.trigger: Automatic silence completion runs setState from a non-React SpeechRecognition 'end' callback. That update has default priority and is not flushed until a later task, so a pointerdown, pointerup and click can all land before the commit. Both the latch and the click closure then still see mode 'stop'.
new_concrete_bugs.impact: It does not send and does not acknowledge Review. The Stop branch sets manualStop=true and calls toggleTap(). The controller is no longer holding, so press() starts a NEW recording where the user meant to stop. manualStop stays true through that new session. If the new session then ends by itself, the gate treats it as manual: reviewNeeded=false and the control goes straight to Send, so the original risk comes back through a chained case. Possible fix: in the Stop branch, act only when hold.view().listening is true (or derive the mode from hold.view() at click time), and set manualStop only when a release really happens.

new_concrete_bugs.trigger: A touch drag-off leaves activationMode set, because implicit capture means no buttons!==0 leave arrives and a tap on iOS does not focus the button, so onBlur does not fire either. A later activation arrives with no fresh pointerdown or keydown, for example an assistive-technology click, in a different mode.
new_concrete_bugs.impact: The mismatch drops one activation silently, and the next one works. It cannot cause a send or a Review acknowledgement.

limits: I reviewed only the attached source and tests. I ran nothing. The reported 326/326, tsc 0 and lint 0 results are not independently verified.

There is no browser or device proof of the pointer event order: iOS Safari compatibility focus and click after pointerup, Android Chrome with pointercancel on pan, and Windows or desktop pointerleave. The touch analysis relies on the Pointer Events implicit-capture rules.
The jsdom tests wrap controller callbacks in act(), which flushes updates at once. They cannot show the render-lag window in the first bug.
While Review is pending, textarea Enter does nothing and shows no feedback. This follows from the design (acknowledge before Send) and is not treated as a defect.
Only voice input was in scope. No TTS, no land and no all-annotation approval were assessed.
